items.name: 503 The request could not be satisfied
items.message: The request could not be satisfied.
items.reasonSummary: Usually appears during a Roblox outage or broader downtime rather than a local gameplay issue.
items.quickFix: Wait a few minutes, retry, and check Roblox server status before changing browser or network settings.

items.name: 504 roblox.com took too long to respond
items.message: roblox.com took too long to respond.
items.reasonSummary: This is typically a web timeout caused by Roblox downtime, heavy load, or a flaky local connection.
items.quickFix: Retry on a stable connection and confirm whether Roblox is having a wider outage.

items.name: Access Denied 403
items.message: You do not have permission to view this page.
items.reasonSummary: The requested Roblox page is restricted, unavailable to the current account, or blocked by the access path being used.
items.quickFix: Sign in with the correct account, open a public page instead, and avoid restricted or moderation-only URLs.
items.notes: This is the website access-denied case, not the newer client initialization article that Roblox Support also labels as 403.

items.name: An error occurred, please try again
items.message: An error occurred, please try again.
items.reasonSummary: PGG associates this website message with invalid IP reputation or certain VPN/proxy paths.
items.quickFix: Disable VPN or proxy software, refresh the page, and try a normal home or mobile network.

items.name: Avatar Page Error
items.message: The avatar page is temporarily unavailable.
items.reasonSummary: This usually points to a temporary Roblox-side issue with the avatar editor or related services.
items.quickFix: Retry later, reload the page, and avoid making repeated outfit changes until the page recovers.

items.name: Bad Request 400
items.message: There was a problem with your request.
items.reasonSummary: The browser sent a malformed or stale request to Roblox, often because of bad cached state or an invalid URL.
items.quickFix: Refresh, clear Roblox cookies for the page, and retry with a clean link.

items.name: Down For Maintenance
items.message: We are making things more awesome. Be back soon.
items.reasonSummary: Roblox has taken part of the site or payments flow offline for maintenance or emergency work.
items.quickFix: Wait for maintenance to finish instead of reinstalling the client or changing device settings.

items.name: Game Pass Loading Error
items.message: Failed to load Game Passes. Please try again later.
items.reasonSummary: The game pass service is not responding cleanly, or the local connection is dropping requests.
items.quickFix: Retry later, refresh the experience page, and test from another network if it keeps failing.

items.name: Internal Server Error 500
items.message: An unexpected error occurred.
items.reasonSummary: Roblox hit a server-side problem while processing the page or action.
items.quickFix: Retry later, and if the same action repeatedly fails, use Roblox support instead of repeated retries.

items.name: Item Owned
items.message: You already own this item.
items.reasonSummary: The purchase flow is blocked because the account already owns the catalog item.
items.quickFix: Check inventory before retrying the purchase; no technical fix is needed.

items.name: Library Error
items.message: Library temporarily unavailable, please try again later.
items.reasonSummary: PGG ties this to bad category values in the URL or a temporary library service issue.
items.quickFix: Retry from a normal library link and remove any invalid category or search parameters from the URL.

items.name: Maximum Friends Error
items.message: That user currently has the max number of friends allowed.
items.reasonSummary: The friend request fails because the target account has reached the platform limit.
items.quickFix: Wait for the other user to free a slot or use followers instead of retrying the same request.

items.name: Page Not Found 404
items.message: Page cannot be found or no longer exists.
items.reasonSummary: The URL is wrong, the page has moved, or the profile or asset behind it was removed.
items.quickFix: Check the URL spelling and try navigating from Roblox search instead of a saved old link.

items.name: Registration Error
items.message: Sorry, an error occurred.
items.reasonSummary: Account creation failed because of Roblox-side signup issues or a bad local network state.
items.quickFix: Retry later, change networks if needed, and avoid reusing obviously invalid username or email inputs.

items.name: Something Went Wrong Error
items.message: An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later.
items.reasonSummary: PGG notes this can appear when the page points at a non-existent Roblox error target or stale page state.
items.quickFix: Reload from a clean URL and retry the action from the normal navigation flow.

items.name: Too Many Redirects
items.message: The page is redirecting improperly or too many times.
items.reasonSummary: This usually means the account or session is bouncing between conflicting Roblox routes; PGG specifically calls out poison-ban cases.
items.quickFix: Clear Roblox cookies, sign in again, and test from a fresh browser profile.

items.name: Unable to Join Private VIP Server
items.message: You cannot join this VIP server because this game is private.
items.reasonSummary: The target VIP server belongs to a private or review-locked experience that the current account cannot access.
items.quickFix: Join a public server, wait for the experience to reopen, or use an allowed account.

items.name: Updating Avatar Error
items.message: Items you do not own are in this outfit.
items.reasonSummary: The saved outfit references traded, sold, deleted, or otherwise unavailable avatar items.
items.quickFix: Remove the unavailable item from the outfit and rebuild the look from currently owned pieces.

items.name: Client Crash
items.message: Roblox needs to quit because of an unexpected error.
items.reasonSummary: Common triggers include low memory, extreme lag, unstable drivers, or starting a game while the client is already in a bad state.
items.quickFix: Close background apps, restart the device, update graphics drivers, and relaunch Roblox cleanly.

items.name: Connection Fail
items.message: Failed to download or apply critical settings.
items.reasonSummary: The launcher lost internet access or failed DNS resolution while it was fetching required Roblox configuration.
items.quickFix: Check internet and DNS stability, then retry after restarting Roblox.

items.name: Error Starting Game
items.message: An error occurred trying to launch the game.
items.reasonSummary: This usually traces back to maintenance, unstable connectivity, or an account that cannot currently enter the experience.
items.quickFix: Retry later, confirm the account is in good standing, and test from another network if needed.
items.notes: PGG also notes an Android-specific version of this startup failure.

items.name: HttpSendRequest Failed
items.message: A connection with the server could not be established.
items.reasonSummary: The client could not complete the HTTP calls Roblox needs during startup.
items.quickFix: Retry on a stable network, disable conflicting security tools temporarily, and relaunch the client.

items.name: Purchase Error
items.message: A purchase failed because the item is offsale, the account lacks Robux, or Roblox hit a temporary checkout issue.
items.reasonSummary: PGG groups several purchase failures under one family of storefront errors.
items.quickFix: Confirm the item is still on sale, make sure enough Robux are available, and retry later if Roblox checkout is unstable.
items.notes: PGG lists subcases for offsale items, insufficient Robux, and generic temporary purchase failures.

items.name: Error Code 6
items.message: An error occurred while starting Roblox. Error Code: 6.
items.reasonSummary: The launcher timed out while downloading an update or opening a game, often because of weak internet or antivirus interference.
items.quickFix: Retry on a stable network, allow Roblox through antivirus or firewall tools, and relaunch the installer if needed.

items.name: Error Code 103
items.message: The Roblox game you are trying to join is currently not available.
items.reasonSummary: PGG associates this mainly with Xbox users trying to join experiences that are only available on PC or mobile.
items.quickFix: Open the experience on a supported platform or choose a console-compatible experience.
items.notes: This is commonly described as an Xbox-specific availability error.

items.name: Error Code 110
items.message: The Roblox experience you are trying to join is currently not available.
items.reasonSummary: PGG ties this to Roblox-side operational issues or outages.
items.quickFix: Retry later and verify server health before reinstalling the client.

items.name: Error Code 256
items.message: Developer has shut down all game servers or the game server has shut down.
items.reasonSummary: The current server was closed intentionally by the developer, a VIP server owner, or an in-game moderation flow.
items.quickFix: Reconnect to a different live server or wait until the developer brings servers back.
items.notes: PGG groups this closely with 274 as a server-shutdown family.

items.name: Error Code 260
items.message: There was a problem receiving data, please reconnect.
items.reasonSummary: The client stopped receiving the data stream it expected from Roblox services.
items.quickFix: Reconnect, restart Roblox, and test the connection on another network if this repeats.

items.name: Error Code 261
items.message: Error while receiving data or problem streaming data, please reconnect.
items.reasonSummary: The session stream broke because of network instability, Roblox downtime, or another transport problem.
items.quickFix: Reconnect, switch networks if available, and retry after checking whether Roblox is down.

items.name: Error Code 262
items.message: There was a problem sending data, please reconnect.
items.reasonSummary: The client could not upload session data back to Roblox, so the experience failed to keep loading.
items.quickFix: Reconnect and retry after stabilizing the network path.

items.name: Error Code 264
items.message: The same account launched the game from a different device.
items.reasonSummary: This happens when the same Roblox account starts the experience on more than one device or when old session state has not cleared.
items.quickFix: Sign out or close Roblox on the other device, then restart and relaunch from a single active session.

items.name: Error Code 266
items.message: Your connection timed out. Check your internet connection and try again.
items.reasonSummary: The session stalled long enough that Roblox treated the client as disconnected or unresponsive.
items.quickFix: Reconnect on a more stable network, restart Roblox, and avoid long AFK periods on weak connections.

items.name: Error Code 267
items.message: You were kicked from this game.
items.reasonSummary: The experience removed the player through a kick, ban, or another server-side rule created by the experience owner.
items.quickFix: Read the in-game reason if one is shown and contact the experience staff if you think the removal was a mistake.
items.notes: Roblox Support separately describes 267 as an experience-level ban path.

items.name: Error Code 268
items.message: You have been kicked due to unexpected client behavior.
items.reasonSummary: This usually points to a client integrity or compatibility problem, though lag, security tools, and exploit detection can all trigger it.
items.quickFix: Reboot, update or reinstall Roblox, remove conflicting overlays or exploit tools, and retry on a stable connection.

items.name: Error Code 270
items.message: Lost connection to Team Create. Please reconnect.
items.reasonSummary: Roblox Studio lost its live Team Create session with the shared place.
items.quickFix: Rejoin Team Create, verify the connection is stable, and restart Studio if the collaboration state does not recover.
items.notes: This is a Studio collaboration error rather than a normal game-session error.

items.name: Error Code 271
items.message: Server was shut down due to no active players / you have been kicked by the server / unable to find instance.
items.reasonSummary: PGG groups several shutdown-style variants under 271, all tied to a server that is closing or no longer accepting the connection.
items.quickFix: Reconnect to a fresh server and avoid retrying the same instance if it is already shutting down.
items.notes: Variant family noted by PGG rather than current Roblox Support.

items.name: Error Code 272
items.message: Disconnected due to the Security Key Mismatch.
items.reasonSummary: PGG associates this with exploit detection or other security validation failures.
items.quickFix: Close any modified clients or exploit tools, relaunch the official client, and reconnect.

items.name: Error Code 273
items.message: Disconnected from the game, possibly because the game was joined from another device.
items.reasonSummary: This is another multi-device session conflict and is often described as a close relative of 264.
items.quickFix: Close the other Roblox session, sign out elsewhere, and reconnect from a single device.
items.notes: PGG notes an overlap with account warnings or bans in some cases.

items.name: Error Code 274
items.message: The game developer has temporarily shut down the server. Please try again.
items.reasonSummary: The server was closed intentionally by the developer or VIP server owner, or the player hit a moderation case during play.
items.quickFix: Reconnect to a different live server or wait until the developer reopens the experience.

items.name: Error Code 275
items.message: Roblox has shut down the server for maintenance. Please try again.
items.reasonSummary: The active server was taken offline for maintenance or because the underlying game state changed.
items.quickFix: Wait for maintenance to finish and then reconnect to a new server.

items.name: Error Code 277
items.message: Lost connection to the game server, please reconnect.
items.reasonSummary: The client did connect, but the live game-server link later broke because of network changes, Wi-Fi drops, or similar instability.
items.quickFix: Reconnect on a stable connection, avoid switching networks mid-session, and reboot the router if the disconnects repeat.

items.name: Error Code 278
items.message: You were disconnected for being idle 20 minutes.
items.reasonSummary: Roblox automatically ends sessions when the player stays AFK for too long.
items.quickFix: Reconnect and keep the session active if you need to remain in the experience.

items.name: Error Code 279
items.message: Failed to connect to the game.
items.reasonSummary: This is the general join failure family for game-server connection attempts and some teleport path errors.
items.quickFix: Check connection quality, retry another server, and update or reinstall Roblox if the failure persists.
items.notes: PGG lists common variants as ID 17 connection failure, ID 146 illegal teleport destination, and ID 148 outdated client.

items.name: Error Code 280
items.message: Your version of Roblox may be out of date. Please update Roblox and try again.
items.reasonSummary: The installed client is behind the required version or local system time and cached state are preventing a clean update.
items.quickFix: Update or reinstall Roblox and verify the device date and time are correct.

items.name: Error Code 403
items.message: Access to www.roblox.com has been denied. You are not authorized to view this page.
items.reasonSummary: Roblox Support ties this newer 403 article to client initialization or launch issues, often involving cached browser state or blocked startup requests.
items.quickFix: Clear temporary browser data, remove VPN or proxy interference, reinstall Roblox, and retry the launch from the website.
items.notes: Different from the website-only access-denied row near the top of this file.

items.name: Error Code 517
items.message: This game is currently unavailable or the game has ended.
items.reasonSummary: The target server is closing, already closed, or no longer available to the client.
items.quickFix: Join a different live server instead of retrying the same closing one.

items.name: Error Code 522
items.message: The user you attempted to join has left the game.
items.reasonSummary: The follow-join target exited the experience before the join request completed.
items.quickFix: Ask the player to rejoin or pick another active server.

items.name: Error Code 523
items.message: The status of the game has changed and you no longer have access.
items.reasonSummary: The experience or server became restricted, private, or unavailable while the join flow was happening.
items.quickFix: Retry later or use an account that still has permission to access the experience.

items.name: Error Code 524
items.message: You do not have permission to join this game.
items.reasonSummary: The current account cannot enter the server because of privacy, invitation, VIP, group, or other access restrictions.
items.quickFix: Check private server permissions, join rules, invitations, and account eligibility before retrying.

items.name: Error Code 529
items.message: An HTTP error has occurred. We are experiencing technical difficulties.
items.reasonSummary: This usually indicates Roblox-side slowdown or partial outage rather than a local gameplay setting issue.
items.quickFix: Close the client, wait, and retry after verifying whether Roblox is under heavy load.

items.name: Error Code 600
items.message: Banned from an Experience.
items.reasonSummary: The experience has banned the current account from joining or rejoining.
items.quickFix: There is no local client fix; appeal to the experience moderators or owner if you believe the ban is wrong.

items.name: Error Code 769
items.message: Teleport failed due to an unexpected error.
items.reasonSummary: An in-experience teleport step failed for a general server or destination reason.
items.quickFix: Retry the teleport flow or rejoin the experience from scratch.

items.name: Error Code 770
items.message: Teleport failed because the root place is inactive, missing, or otherwise invalid.
items.reasonSummary: The destination place is not live, was deleted, or cannot currently accept teleports.
items.quickFix: Retry only after the destination place is active again, or send players to a valid place ID.
items.notes: PGG groups multiple subcases under 770, including inactive and non-existent destinations.

items.name: Error Code 771
items.message: Teleport failed because the server is no longer available.
items.reasonSummary: The target teleport server disappeared before the client could enter it.
items.quickFix: Retry the teleport and choose a fresh server target.

items.name: Error Code 772
items.message: Teleport failed because the server is full.
items.reasonSummary: The destination instance has no open player slots.
items.quickFix: Retry later or teleport to a different server instance.

items.name: Error Code 773
items.message: Teleport failed because the destination game is unapproved or restricted.
items.reasonSummary: The destination place has not been approved, is restricted, or the current player is not allowed to join it.
items.quickFix: Send players to an approved public destination or adjust access permissions before retrying.

items.name: Failed to Load Library
items.message: Roblox Error: Failed to Load Library.
items.reasonSummary: Roblox could not load a required local library or dependency, usually because the install is corrupted or a system component is missing or blocked.
items.quickFix: Reinstall Roblox cleanly, clear leftover local Roblox files, and repair blocked or missing Windows dependencies if the issue persists.
items.notes: Roblox Support surfaces this under Reporting Bugs rather than the general numbered error-code list.
